# Reserved words, generated from the patterns in scope. Do not edit.
#
# Most of this is ADVICE now. A name may contain any of these words: a
# statement with two readings is an error that offers the bracketings, so
# nothing is refused at the declaration for what it might do to a reading.
# Using a word here still costs a bracket wherever the two meanings meet.
#
# Two sections are still rules, and say so: no name may BEGIN with the words
# of an anchor-only pattern, because those readings are not all reachable by
# bracketing; and no pattern may use a word operator or an injection word.
# Adding a line to either is a breaking change for every program that sees it.
#
# A pattern below is written as it is declared, and «guillemets» mark the one
# thing that cannot be: a PINNED hole, which takes one word and has no
# declaration syntax yet. Everything outside them is ordinary source.

## COSTS A BRACKET INSIDE A NAME (0) — advice


## NO PATTERN MAY USE (2) — a word operator, everywhere, in every scope

    is           reads as an operator between two values, so a pattern using it would tie
    otherwise    reads as an operator between two values, so a pattern using it would tie

## COSTS NOTHING (1) — every hole before a word is determinate

    for each «one word, or a bracketed name» in (_)

## NO NAME MAY BEGIN WITH (0) — a rule, not advice


## PROTECTED (3) — no pattern may use these as glue

    old          builds old «a name», and is refused in any segment, not only glue
    index        builds index of «a loop variable»
    of           builds index of «a loop variable»

## INJECTED (2) — names the compiler builds, and never asks anyone to rename

    old «a name»                 the previous value of a mutable declaration
    index of «a loop variable»   a loop's counter
